proposals.evidence: CDIAL 5020 chādi explicitly gives Sindhi/Lahnda/Punjabi chāī ashes, Assamese sāi and Bengali chāi, as well as Hindi chāī. The selected cāī/caī/chai/tʃhai/tśai/ʦaī survey forms fit this ash noun, with initial aspiration and affricate notation retained as regional/transcription qualifications. The source ash/ashes distinction and local transmission remain open. Exact response: cāī.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11109 leṭyati gives Lahnda leṭaṇ, Punjabi/Western Pahari leṭṇā, Nepali leṭnu and Hindi leṭnā lie down. The selected bare leṭ and simple leṭa/leṭo responses use this stem; leṭṇā is an ordinary infinitive explicitly documented by the entry. Mixed imperative/past elicitation labels and source final vowels are retained. The proposed deeper non-Aryan connection and local Indo-Aryan transmission remain unresolved. Exact response: leṭṇā.
